source_text: Finito autem prooemio, ubi etiam laborasti, sicut soles, probare quod praedico, "Deum esse hominum conditorem"; mea deinde verba proponis, ubi dixi: "Mundo, non Deo nasci hominem, qui de concupiscentia carnis nascitur; Deo autem nasci cum ex aqua et spiritu renascitur" … Quibus meis verbis sic insidiaris, ut asseras hinc intellegi me debere dixisse, quod ad diabolum pertineat quidquid ad mundum pertinet: quia scilicet alibi dixeram, "eos qui de corporum commixtione nascuntur ad ius diaboli pertinere"; asserendo utique, "de potestate erui tenebrarum, cum regenerantur in Christo".
pass_a_gloss: The preface having been finished, where you also laboured, as you are wont, to prove what I preach, 'God to be the founder of men'; then you set forth my words, where I said: 'To the world, not to God, is born the man who is born of the concupiscence of the flesh; but to God he is born when he is reborn of water and spirit'. These my words you so ambush, that you assert that from here I must be understood to have said that whatever pertains to the world pertains to the devil: because namely elsewhere I had said 'those who are born of the mingling of bodies to pertain to the right of the devil'; asserting of course 'to be snatched from the power of darkness when they are regenerated in Christ'.

lemmas.gloss: you lie in wait for, lay a trap

pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “After finishing your preface, in which you labored, as you usually do, to prove what I myself preach, ‘that God is the maker of human beings,’ you then set out my words, where I said: ‘A human being who is born of the desire of the flesh is born to the world, not to God; but he is born to God when he is reborn of water and the Spirit.’”

“You lie in wait for these words of mine so as to assert that it must be understood from them that I said that whatever belongs to the world belongs to the devil, because, of course, I had said elsewhere ‘that those who are born from the union of bodies belong to the devil’s jurisdiction,’ asserting, that is, that they ‘are rescued from the power of darkness when they are reborn in Christ.’”

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
